headline_marked: Apple unveils new Mac Mini and Mac Studio with [[M6 and M5 Ultra chips]]
headline: Apple unveils new Mac Mini and Mac Studio with M6 and M5 Ultra chips
summary: Apple's latest Mac Mini and Mac Studio updates feature new M6 and M5 Ultra processors, with preorders now open and shipping starting September 22nd.
details: Apple has officially announced two new processors, the M6 and M5 Ultra, powering updated versions of its Mac Mini and Mac Studio desktop computers. These new machines are available for preorder, with most configurations set to ship starting September 22nd, 2026.

The Mac Mini now starts at $899, a significant $300 increase from the previous M4-equipped model. The Mac Studio maintains its starting price of $2,499 for the M5 Max model, but configurations with higher RAM and storage options are also available.

The Mac Mini with the M6 chip starts at $899, while the M5 Pro version begins at $1,699. This update brings substantial processor upgrades to Apple's compact desktop, alongside improved connectivity including 2.5Gb Ethernet, Bluetooth 6, and Wi-Fi 7.

The updated Mac Studio starts at $2,499 for the M5 Max chip configuration with 36GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage. The M5 Ultra version, featuring 96GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD, starts at $5,499.

While base models are scheduled for September 22nd delivery, configurations equipped with up to 512GB of RAM will see availability extended to late October, with pricing for these high-end options yet to be announced.

headline_marked: Perplexity launches [[Portable Computer]] for fully local AI agent tasks
headline: Perplexity launches Portable Computer for fully local AI agent tasks
summary: New platform runs AI models and user data entirely on local hardware, starting with Nvidia DGX Spark and RTX GPUs, with zero cloud costs.
details: Perplexity has launched Portable Computer, a new platform designed to run its agentic AI tasks entirely on local hardware. This move, developed in partnership with Nvidia, aims to bring complex AI workloads off the cloud and onto user devices, starting with Nvidia's DGX Spark desktop supercomputer and Linux machines equipped with Nvidia RTX GPUs.

The core benefit of Portable Computer is that the AI model, user files, and the work itself remain on the user's machine. This means tasks completed locally incur no billing credits. By default, all operations begin on the device, with the system only seeking permission to use more powerful cloud-based models for specific steps.

Nvidia sees this as a strategic shift, signaling that local AI has become practical beyond hobbyist use. The company is keen to supply the hardware for this growing market. "Local AI reached an inflection point," stated Nvidia's director of developer technology, highlighting the emergence of useful open-source models that don't require extreme quantization.

Perplexity Computer, the company's existing knowledge work platform, orchestrates AI models, files, and tools for multi-step tasks. Portable Computer replicates this functionality locally, packaging the models, agent harness, inference engine, tools, and connectors into a single, easy-to-set-up system, eliminating the historical pain of manually assembling local AI stacks.

A demonstration showcased the system handling sensitive financial documents locally, reviewing investment files without uploading them to the cloud. Using a 27-billion-parameter Qwen model on a DGX Spark, the agent identified unnecessary fees, with the cloud credit counter remaining at zero.

The platform also supports hybrid workflows, as seen in another demo where an agent analyzed user funnel data locally and then pushed the results to Slack via Perplexity's connectors. This demonstrates that local-first operation does not mean isolation, with integrations for Google Drive, Gmail, and GitHub also available.

At launch, Portable Computer supports Qwen 3.8 27B and Perplexity's own PPLX 27B models, with Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning coming soon. The minimum hardware requirement is an RTX GPU with at least 24GB of VRAM, such as a GeForce RTX 3090 or newer, balancing performance with broad availability.

Portable Computer is available today for Pro, Max, Enterprise Pro, and Enterprise Max subscribers on Linux, with Windows support expected in September. Perplexity also published research emphasizing the need for tight integration between local AI models and their agent harnesses for effective operation.
